description.summary: Semantic Chunking splits source content around meaning-oriented boundaries so chunks can preserve topical coherence.
description.description: Semantic Chunking is a RAG technique that divides content using semantic similarity, topic shifts, embedding-based grouping, or other meaning-oriented boundary signals.
description.problemStatement: Size-based chunking can produce retrieval units that are uniform but not aligned with the topics or meaning carried by the source content.
description.coreIdea: Use semantic signals to group related content together and separate content when the topic or meaning changes enough to justify a boundary.

inputRequirements.name: Source content with semantic boundary signals
inputRequirements.description: Documents or text content that should be divided according to meaning-oriented boundaries.

outputArtifacts.name: Semantic chunks
outputArtifacts.description: Chunk artifacts grouped around topical or semantic coherence rather than only uniform size.

implementationConsiderations: Account for higher computation and model or configuration dependence when deriving semantic boundaries.
Track chunking configuration because semantic grouping can be less deterministic than simple splitting strategies.
evaluationGuidance: Evaluate whether semantic chunks improve retrieved context coherence compared with simpler chunking baselines.
